items.item: A critic review that meets a refused or resting credential (no other credential may serve it) does not wait: it becomes an escalate verdict (or a review-failed card when the critic throws), the person gets a second card beside the refused card, and the review never runs by itself at the reset or after a new key.

Neither consults credentialWaitOf. Same place as R-criticbudget. ADR 0100 points 9 and 12 ('the work that needs it waits').

items.item: Rebuilds that could not run (busy or dirty worktree, failed step) are remembered only in memory: a squash-merge or close seen while the dependent's worktree was busy, followed by a restart, is never rebuilt, so the dependent's PR keeps the dependency's commits and files.

items.item: No shared worktree lock: a merge already under way when a dependency closes can still finish before the rebuild pushes, and ReviewedPrMerge's own git steps in a task worktree (the update path of mergeChecked) are not serialised with a rebuild of that worktree.
items.evidence: Verified: pr-executor.ts:300-321 worktreesInUse/inWorktree/tryWorktree are private to the module; loop/merge.ts:361, :530 and :826 build GitOps on the task worktree without them; the rebuild voids the record first (dependent-branches.ts:213 settleRecord) but does not stop a host merge call already started. items.item: Chain of three: if the middle task's worktree is busy when the first is squash-merged, the third follows the rebuilt middle through rebuiltTo and is not rebuilt, so its PR keeps the first task's pre-squash commits and files (the U-028 symptom) until the middle merges.

items.item: U-078: under 'Wait' a refused credential's work waits, a refused API key's included (beyond the session lead's default, which named only a refused subscription).

items.question: Under 'Wait', should a refused credential's work wait for a new one, or move to the other credential?

(c) move only when the other costs no money (a refused key's work goes to the subscription); a refused subscription waits

new_areas.title: Leftovers of wave 7, run side: same-titled tasks never share a branch, a review refused at a budget pauses instead of failing, and the merge, rebuild, take-out and copy paths keep true state across busy worktrees, crashes and redos
problems: [major] Two tasks with the same title created in one repository within about 65 s get the same branch fr/<first 8 hex of the UUIDv7>-<slug>; the second finds the first's open pull request by branch name, resumes it and pushes its own work onto it. Evidence: Verified at fa1a86f. packages/capabilities/src/githost/pr-executor.ts:667-670 branch = fr/${task.id.slice(0, 8)}-<slug> (no deps.branchFor is wired anywhere); packages/platform/src/ids.ts:4-14 newId puts the top 32 bits of the 48-bit ms timestamp in those 8 hex characters, so they change only every 65,536 ms. pr-executor.ts:708-711 looks the open PR up by head branch alone, :720 sets resume, :743-745 checks out origin/<branch>, :908 pushes with force and :2176-2186 updates the first task's PR. Polish problems[33] (C-59, no id on screen) must keep the name unique.

[major] A critic review refused at the project's budget counts as a failed try: the review becomes an 'escalate' verdict, the retry ladder runs up to 4 times and files '"X" failed 4 times' instead of pausing the task at the project's budget. Evidence: Verified at fa1a86f. packages/critic/src/critic.ts:519-526 gives outcome budget_exceeded (runOutcomeOf :1139-1148) when no verdict was captured; buildVerdict :713-724 then sets verdict 'escalate' with the high finding 'Critic review did not complete (budget_exceeded)'. packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:2955-3018 (reviewTask) emits it as an ordinary critic.verdict and :1880-1990 hands it to the ladder; nothing maps an outer-limit refusal of the review to the paused outcome that the owner's budgets decision ('paused outcome (no review, no failed try)') and ADR 0112 point 6 require. packages/runtime/test/budget-pause.test.ts:148-160 already takes projectBudgetUsdMicro.

[minor] A critic review that meets a refused or resting credential (no other credential may serve it) does not wait: it becomes an escalate verdict (or a review-failed card when the critic throws), the person gets a second card beside the refused card, and the review never runs by itself at the reset or after a new key. Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/agent/loop.ts:692-704 throws USAGE_LIMIT_CODE/provider_auth, outcomeFor :1199-1210 makes it 'error', critic.ts:713-724 turns any run without a verdict into 'escalate'; runner.ts:1902-1966 files fileReviewFailedRequest for a thrown review. Neither consults credentialWaitOf. Same place as R-criticbudget. ADR 0100 points 9 and 12 ('the work that needs it waits').

[minor] Under 'Wait' the session ends at the first task that must wait and skips the rest of the queue, including tasks whose first usable credential can serve now; the project-level wait label is put on every ready task. Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:1768-1777 pushes the whole queue onto skipped and stops with CREDENTIAL_WAIT_STOP at the first credentialWait; packages/runtime/src/daemon/task-words.ts:610-615 gives every ready task ctx.credentialWait (credentialWaitRow, task-display.ts:101-127). ADR 0100 point 10 (docs/decisions/0100:176-190): only tasks 'whose first choice it is' wait. A bug under either answer to the U-078 owner question.

[minor] A crash or app close in the middle of a run leaves uncommitted files in the task's worktree with no work-in-progress commit; the next run carries them over, or git refuses its checkout ('untracked working tree files would be overwritten'). Evidence: Verified: pr-executor.ts:661-821 executeIn never checks git.status().dirty before the resume checkout (:743-745) or createBranch (:821, 'checkout -B', git.ts:439); the work-in-progress save (:830-835) and the leftovers set aside run only after inner.execute returns. W6-24 again, for crashes.

[minor] The merge retry pass and the start-up resume: a merge they make posts no Inbox Update or notification (design §3.8), and every retry of a waiting record is a full gated merge_pr call (its own token, one audit row, about 5 GitHub calls) per record per minute for up to 1440 tries. Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/daemon/compose.ts:2508-2511 onMerged only logs and emits a project refresh; packages/runtime/src/loop/merge.ts:884-905 retryWaiting -> mergeRecorded -> run (:1120-1180: ownToken tokens.issue at :1160, mayMerge :685-741 reads no checks), beforeToolCall :1303-1305 writes the audit row; MAX_MERGE_ATTEMPTS :84 = 1440; resumeAtStart :913-950 files nothing. ADR 0111:246-249 known gap.

[minor] After a crash the session page reads 'Interrupted: Forerunner closed: nothing done. CHF 0.00.' and the Overview 'No session yet', although its task was accepted and its PR merged later. Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/session/recovery.ts:139-143 session.ended payload carries only status, stopReason and released (no completed count, no spentUsdMicro), so event-lines.ts:267-282 says 'nothing done' and CHF 0.00; runner.ts:2680 is the only writer of summary_cache.last_session, so SummaryTab.tsx:177 shows 'No session yet.'.

[minor] A session whose tasks all paused at their budgets gets 'Session review: sent back for changes (grade 70, 2 findings)' with the finding 'No planned task was done: N of N wait for the person'. Evidence: Verified: runner.ts:2048-2072 moves a paused task to needs_human; packages/critic/src/session-review.ts:296-327 counts it as plannedWaiting and adds the medium finding, which leads to revise. The '(s)' summary (:590-592) is polish (PA-reviewplural).

[minor] The card filed when a rebuild voids a review is merge-record's left-open card: 'I merged it' (primary) and 'Leave it open'. 'I merged it' notes 'merged by you' on the task while the PR is still open; the body says 'or send it back' with no button; neither Merge nor Redo is offered. Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/session/dependent-branches.ts:294-305 calls fileLeftOpenRequest with no options, so loop/merge.ts:1679/:1710 MERGE_LEFT_OPEN_OPTIONS apply; session/pr-answers.ts:98 and :197-202 patch the task reason 'merged by you: <url>' without asking the host; request-words.ts:845-853 makes the first option primary; body text dependent-branches.ts:84.

[minor] Rebuilds that could not run (busy or dirty worktree, failed step) are remembered only in memory: a squash-merge or close seen while the dependent's worktree was busy, followed by a restart, is never rebuilt, so the dependent's PR keeps the dependency's commits and files. Evidence: Verified: dependent-branches.ts:108-109 owed is an in-memory Map, filled by rebuildFor (:194-206); sweep (:177-190) refinds only dependencies that are not done. ADR 0111:182-184 known gap.

[minor] No shared worktree lock: a merge already under way when a dependency closes can still finish before the rebuild pushes, and ReviewedPrMerge's own git steps in a task worktree (the update path of mergeChecked) are not serialised with a rebuild of that worktree. Evidence: Verified: pr-executor.ts:300-321 worktreesInUse/inWorktree/tryWorktree are private to the module; loop/merge.ts:361, :530 and :826 build GitOps on the task worktree without them; the rebuild voids the record first (dependent-branches.ts:213 settleRecord) but does not stop a host merge call already started. ADR 0111:183-184.

[minor] Chain of three: if the middle task's worktree is busy when the first is squash-merged, the third follows the rebuilt middle through rebuiltTo and is not rebuilt, so its PR keeps the first task's pre-squash commits and files (the U-028 symptom) until the middle merges. Evidence: Verified: pr-executor.ts:1428-1429 tryWorktree skips the busy middle; heldState (:1220-1257) maps the third's old middle sha through rebuiltTo (:1268) and counts it as open, so the third is not rebuilt.

[minor] A redo's new PR moves a merged merge record back to queued outside the state graph and clears its take-out fields: Redo is offered while a take-out PR is open, and that PR is then no longer listed or settled. Evidence: Verified: packages/state/src/repos/merge-record.ts:36-62 pin patches a merged record to 'queued' for a different pr_url without assertTransition and nulls take_out_pr_number/url/state; packages/state/src/workflow.ts:103 'merged: []' and docs/maintainers/data-model.md:152 'merged -> (terminal)'; apps/ui/src/lib/task-actions.ts:105-107 offers Redo unless takeOut.state is 'offered'; packages/state/test/suite.ts:2442-2463 has no different-URL case. ADR 0113:199-201 known gap.

[minor] Take this work out on a dependent PR that GitHub merged with a merge commit carrying its dependency's commits reverts the merge whole with -m 1, so the dependency's work goes too. Evidence: Verified: pr-executor.ts:2245-2254 takeOutPlan returns {how:'merge', commits:[mergeSha], mainline:true} for any two-parent commit, without checking whether the merged side holds another task's record's commits. ADR 0113:201-204. Only after a merge made on GitHub out of dependency order.

[minor] No conflict notice: an open task PR whose mergeable turned false after another merge is never noticed; the Overview row keeps offering Merge and no card is filed (merge-in-app fix_scope 6 acceptance unmet). Evidence: Verified: compose.ts:4108-4112 passes open PRs to dependentBranches.pullRequestState, which returns at once for state open (dependent-branches.ts:120); mergeable=false is read only when Merge is pressed (loop/merge.ts:437-449). ADR 0111:246-249.

[minor] Each Overview read of a repository project makes 4 GitHub calls (listPullRequests, getRepo, getBranchRules per base) with no cache, and while a row settles (waiting_checks can last a day) the Overview reads again on every card change, other projects' included. Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/daemon/pull-requests.ts:257 listPullRequests and :653-678 rulesOf (getRepo + getBranchRules) on every view; apps/ui/src/pages/project/SummaryTab.tsx:372-376 reloads on every card while settling.current is set.

[minor] In the automatic merge mode a queued record without the person's approval reads 'merging' on the Overview but 'Accepted · waiting for you to merge' on the Tasks row; the retry merges it by itself, so the Tasks words are untrue. Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/daemon/task-words.ts:417-419 returns 'waiting for you to merge' for any non-person queued record and ignores the mode; pull-requests.ts:183-186 reads the mode (after_review gives merging).

[minor] The repository offer and the chat's repo_create can both be open for one repository (at any level, Autopilot too); nothing withdraws the offer once a repository is linked, so its 'Create the repository' then fails with a warning. The chat card is generic: titled 'a GitHub repository for X' with lowercase yes/no. Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/loop/repo-create.ts:302-303 dedupes only its own repo:create: key; repoCreatePrefix appears only in request-words.ts:1133, request-answers.ts:86/:483 and repo-create.ts:44 (no withdrawal); packages/commands/src/commands/repo.ts:89-101 builds the card with no ask, so genericCard (request-words.ts:1041-1075) keeps 'yes'/'no'; the offer's sync then runs repo.create, which refuses ('already has a repository', repo.ts:97).

[minor] When this computer's copy cannot be brought to what is merged (a tracked file the person edited is changed by a merge, an ignored file in the way, a 'local only/' path in another case on Windows), Files keeps 'As merged on GitHub, updated HH:MM' and never says why it stopped following. Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/loop/docs.ts:716-724 and compose.ts:2461-2470 only log 'this computer's copy of the repository not refreshed'; CopyView (docs.ts:200-205) has no field for a copy that stopped following. ADR 0113 'Known limits'.

[minor] A reused task worktree keeps '/Local only/' in .git/info/exclude after the repository starts tracking a folder named Local only, so new files the agent writes there are silently left out of the commit. Evidence: Verified: packages/capabilities/src/githost/local-only.ts:92-112 excludeNeverPushed only appends lines; pr-executor.ts:679-681 passes [TRY_DIR] once origin/<base> tracks Local only/, but never removes the earlier line.

[minor] The session log's start line is emitted before the executor picks: after a web hand-over (page reader off) it names the planned specialist instead of the one that ran (W5-20), and when the billing pick then waits, 'The writer started "X"' precedes the wait line although nothing ran. Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:1508-1519 emits task.started with runItem.specialist before executor.execute; packages/runtime/src/session/executor.ts:958-971 hands the task to pick.name (reachable only with FORERUNNER_WEB_FETCH=off since d297f97); the billing pick (executor.ts:932) and the wait line (runner.ts:1760-1764) come after.

[minor] The task drawer lists a run that a refused key or a usage limit stopped as 'Failed', although the task went back to ready. Evidence: Verified (moved from polish_add: the words exist, the state is wrong): packages/runtime/src/session/executor.ts:1466-1477 writes result.outcome ('error') to the run row before the credential stop is decided (:1500-1552); task-display.ts:241-243 maps error to 'Failed'; 'Stopped at the usage limit' (:235-236) is never reached for a credential stop (runner.ts:1753-1777 puts the task back to ready).

[minor] The plan card shows the bounded plan guess while the Start dialog shows that figure times the learned ratio, so after a few tasks of a kind the two screens give different amounts for the same tasks. Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/session/intake.ts:1373 and :2450-2464 store boundedPlanEstimate on the plan's tasks; packages/runtime/src/session/start-check.ts:2 scales through EstimatePort/planEstimateUsdMicro. Person items must stay 0 (cost fixup notes[2]).

[minor] Chat turns pay the 1.25x cache-write price on their history with no cache read across turns: the newest user message carries the volatile preamble but the stored history keeps the turn without it, so the next turn's prefix differs. Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:797-801 sends `${context.volatile}\n\n${req.text}` last, historyMessages(earlier) replays the stored text; agent/loop.ts:650 marks {system, tools, messages}. bench-api: turns 2 and 3 each read 5,615 tokens (system and tools) and wrote 749 and 453. The comment at agent.ts:793-795 claims the earlier turns stay cached.

[minor] Test paths that never reach the case they are meant to: the bench stand-in planner leaves the person's questions out of firstSession.items (it hid review blocking 2); e2e 'Stop now asks once' takes its 'already Done' branch under load; the chainOf notAccepted row and Files after a task PR's in-app Merge have no boundary case. Evidence: Verified: testenv/src/bench/plans.ts:564 filters specialist !== 'person' (live replies list it at 0: packages/runtime/test/fixtures/intake-live1.json); apps/ui/e2e/session.spec.ts:79-87 branches on stop.count() while the fake session ends after eventDelayMs 150 per event (fake-daemon.ts:955); 'which is not accepted yet' (pull-requests.ts:410-415) appears in no test; real-daemon.test.ts:8483-8547 never reads GET /projects/:id/files after the chain Merge. mobile-pairing/setup-assistant flakes not reproduced.

Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:2404-2407 stores stopCapChfMicro = usdToChfMicro(stopCapUsdMicro) whenever stopLimitWords(stopReason) is non-null, budget_plan included; stop-words.ts:101-102 ignores the amount for the plan share.

new_areas.fix_scope: One commit per problem, the failing test first, the two majors first (group 4's: the branch name, then the review refused at the project's budget, which shares its fix with the credential case: a critic run that a limit or a credential refused is a pause or a wait, never a verdict). The branch name keeps no id on screen (polish C-59) but must be unique per task (more of the id, or the id's random part). The retry pass reads the checks before it issues a token, and files the Update itself from loop/merge.ts (not compose.ts, which is leftovers7-web's). Persist owed rebuilds on the merge record or the task. One exported worktree lock for pr-executor and ReviewedPrMerge. Owner questions O-waitsecond and O-refusedwait do not block R-waitqueue (a bug under either answer). problems: [major] The open-web agent browser drops Chromium's own sandbox after any first launch failure (a profile lock, a timeout), not only a sandbox one, and keeps running without it for the rest of the process; the log says it runs without the sandbox whatever the cause. Evidence: Verified: packages/capabilities/src/browser/profile.ts:328-340: the catch around the chromiumSandbox:true launch sets unsandboxed for every error (launchRefusal :184-191 only picks a line) and every later launch uses chromiumSandbox:false (W6-30). A silent loss of a security boundary on the browser that reads any public site.

[minor] The site rule fails open: a stored 'Only these websites' whose entries the clean-up no longer accepts reads as 'any public website'. Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/wiring/web-access.ts:437-438 only = cleanSiteList(...).sites; mode = 'only' only while an entry survives, else 'any'. Never entries are kept as written (blockEntry :452-455). Not reachable through settings.set today; a PUBLIC_SUFFIXES or LOCAL_SUFFIX change or a value written by another install (shared store) would widen research silently.

[minor] On the subscription, a built-in file read (Read, NotebookRead, Grep) gets updatedToolOutput as a bare string: Claude Code ignores or rejects the shape, so repository text reaches Claude without the 'information, not instructions' envelope, and a hook error may be logged on every file read. Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/agent/sdk.ts:788-797 marks Read/NotebookRead/Grep untrusted (repo_file; isRepoReadCcTool :1018-1019); :838-842 sends updatedToolOutput: builtInOutput(...), which returns the bare wrapped string for any tool but WebSearch and WebFetch (:897-907). The comment at :824-825 says a file read is 'not changed'. ADR 0107:307-309. No test asserts Read's PostToolUse return.

[minor] On the subscription, what Claude Code still reports after a stop is not booked: a killed run's late messages are never read, and after Stop all revokes the run's token a late booking fails and is only logged, so the ledger and the plan share miss the run's tail. Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/agent/sdk.ts:578-583 returns the iterator without draining on 'killed'; :636-650 catches a failed late booking and logs 'a stopped run's late message was not booked'; packages/runtime/src/enforcement/hooks.ts:248-250 afterModelCall verifies the (revoked) token before it records.

[minor] On the subscription, Claude Code's modelUsage totals, summed over every model (subagents, Haiku auxiliary calls), are booked at the run model's price. Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/agent/sdk.ts:1063-1081 resultTotals adds every model's tokens into one Usage; :396-402 books usageLeft(total, usage) through book(), which prices with req.pricing.cost (:296-300), the run model's price.

[minor] After a change from the Overview, the 'Research reads:' line keeps the value it set, so a later change made in chat (Talk on the Overview) leaves the line stale while the page is open. Evidence: Verified: apps/ui/src/pages/project/SummaryTab.tsx:247-252 line = changed ?? project?.researchReads; changed is set at :284 and never cleared.

[minor] A wait on a refused API key stays until that key is replaced: if the person adds a subscription instead, the ready tasks still read 'Waits for a new API key' and nothing starts by itself, although Start would run them on the subscription. Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/daemon/task-display.ts:101-127 credentialWaitRow labels the project from any source that keeps it in limits.waiting and is refused, without asking whether a pick serves now; wiring/billing-pick.ts:784-813 takeReady keeps the list while the refusal stands; credentialSaved('subscription') (:826) ends only the subscription's refusal; with no order set task runs put the subscription first (docs/decisions/0100:58-60).

Evidence: Verified: packages/runtime/src/daemon/compose.ts:3391-3416 taskBilling.takeReady() removes the entries, then scheduler.request(); the scheduler's queue is in memory and a background start that fails is only logged (packages/runtime/src/session/triggers.ts:428-450).
